headline: Preprint reports that incomplete tool-output wording can cause agent overclaims and verifier errors
summary: An arXiv paper reports a paired study of four ways tool-output formatters can misrepresent search scope, result completeness, uncertainty or identifier provenance in one production RAG archive system. Across three model families and 32 holdout cases, the authors report that repaired wording reduced unsupported agent claims for the first three defect families; in a fixed-answer verifier test, false answers were accepted 30/30 times under warped wording and 0/30 under clear wording for scope, completeness and uncertainty. Results are author-reported and limited to the studied cases, models and prompts; identifier-provenance wording had a much smaller effect. The paper also links an offline artifact and two upstream formatter/tool fixes: the cited OpenClaw fix is merged, while the Hermes truncation fix remains an open pull request. These code changes do not independently reproduce the paper results or estimate prevalence.
